title: Aurora Glass — Stillwater
prompt: Design a premium landing page for "Stillwater", a fictional breathing and meditation app, in refined glassmorphism. Background: deep midnight (#070b1f) with three slow-drifting aurora ribbons rendered on a canvas (layered, sine-deformed gradient bands in teal #2de2c4, violet #7b5cff and rose #ff6fa8, additive blending, very soft) over a faint twinkling star field. Foreground: frosted-glass panels (backdrop-filter blur + saturate, 1px inner highlight border, subtle grain) — a hero with a large, airy, light-weight sans headline; a centred "breathing orb" that expands and contracts on a 4-7-8 rhythm with a caption that cross-fades Inhale / Hold / Exhale; a row of three feature cards; a testimonial strip; and a pricing section whose monthly/yearly toggle animates a sliding glass pill. Delight: cards tilt in 3D toward the pointer with a moving specular glare; the aurora bends gently toward the cursor. Interaction: hover/tilt cards; click the orb to start/stop a guided one-minute session with a progress ring; pricing toggle. Mobile: cards stack, the orb stays hero-centred.

title: Neon Rain
prompt: Create an immersive cyberpunk street at night titled "NEON RAIN — District 9 Night Market" (fictional). A full-viewport canvas scene with four parallax layers of skyline silhouettes (#05010f → #1a0433) and randomly lit windows; holographic vertical signs with katakana-like glyphs drawn in canvas that flicker with believable neon failure (brief dropouts, buzz); a wet street reflecting the signs (mirrored, blurred, rippled); dense diagonal rain with splash particles on the ground. Palette: hot magenta #ff2a6d, cyan #05d9e8 and acid-yellow #f9f002 accents on ink black. Overlay a thin HUD: time, temperature, "SIGNAL" bars and a scrolling ticker of fictional news in monospace. Typography: condensed uppercase sans with chromatic-aberration text-shadow. Interaction: the pointer moves the parallax camera; a click triggers a lightning flash that briefly lights the whole skyline plus a thunder rumble (Web Audio noise, after a gesture, with a mute toggle); a toggle switches rain intensity. Must stay fluid at 60fps using pooled particles.

title: Raster — Swiss Poster Machine
prompt: Build "RASTER — Swiss Poster Machine", an homage to the International Typographic Style. The page is a single poster on an off-white (#f2efe8) sheet set on a strict 12-column modular grid (revealable with the G key or a toggle that shows hairline cyan grid lines). Palette strictly signal red #e30613, black #111 and white. A heavy grotesque sans stack ("Helvetica Neue", Helvetica, Arial, "Nimbus Sans", sans-serif) used with extreme scale contrast: a giant numeral or word, small flush-left body text, rotated captions. Geometric elements (circles, bars, quarter-arcs) occupy grid cells. Every click (or Space) recomposes the poster from a new seed — elements slide and rotate to new cells with crisp eased FLIP-style transitions, never overlapping text illegibly. Show the seed as an edition mark ("No. 0417"). A small control strip: previous/next composition, grid toggle, invert (black ground). It must look like a museum-quality, Müller-Brockmann-inspired print at any viewport, reflowing the grid for portrait phones.

title: The Clockmaker's Orrery
prompt: Create "The Clockmaker's Orrery", an interactive mechanical model of the solar system in the style of an 18th-century brass instrument. Parchment background (#efe3c6 with a subtle radial vignette and paper fibres from layered gradients), deep ink lines (#2b1d0e), and brass/gold metallic gradients (#b8860b → #f3d27a → #7a5410) for arms, rings and gears. Centre: a glowing sun; eight planets on brass arms orbiting at correct relative orbital periods (Mercury 0.241 y … Neptune 164.8 y) with log-compressed distances; an engraved zodiac ring with degree ticks around the edge; interlocking gears in a corner that rotate in sync with simulated time. Typography: engraved-looking serif small caps ("Iowan Old Style", "Palatino Linotype", Palatino, "P052", Georgia, serif) with generous letter-spacing. UI: a brass-styled readout of the simulated date, a speed dial (pause, 1 day/s, 1 month/s, 1 year/s), and click-a-planet to open an ornate cartouche with its name, period and a short engraved description. Delight: optional tiny ticking sound (Web Audio, after a gesture) and hover glints on the brass. SVG for the instrument, requestAnimationFrame for motion.

title: Sumi — Ink in Water
prompt: Make "Sumi — Ink in Water", a meditative fluid simulation. A full-screen canvas showing warm washi paper (#f4efe6 with procedurally generated fibre noise). Clicking or tapping drops ink that blooms, curls and diffuses like sumi ink in water — implement a small grid-based stable-fluids solver (advection, diffusion, pressure projection) at reduced resolution with smooth upscaling, or an equivalent dye-advection approach; dragging the pointer stirs the water. Default ink is deep sumi black-indigo (#1b1f2a); a minimal vertical toolbar on the right, set in a quiet serif, switches to indigo (#2c3e75), vermillion (#d23c26) or pale gold (#b89b5e). A red hanko seal in the corner (SVG, carved-looking characters approximated with geometric strokes) signs the piece; a "Still the water" button slowly fades the ink away. Typography: an elegant vertical title using writing-mode: vertical-rl. Delight: an occasional falling ink droplet when idle; ink leaves faint tidelines at its edges. Must run smoothly on laptops and lower its resolution on mobile.

title: Loud House Records — Issue 07
prompt: Design "LOUD HOUSE RECORDS — Issue 07", a neo-brutalist web zine for a fictional independent record label. Raw, confident and loud: flat saturated colours (cobalt #1d3cff, electric yellow #ffe600, black #000, off-white #f7f5f0, one hit of hot pink #ff3ea5), 3–4px black borders everywhere, hard offset shadows (8px 8px 0 #000) with no blur, oversized uppercase grotesk headlines, monospace metadata, and a deliberately collaged layout on a visible grid. Sections: a massive masthead with a marquee strip of release names; a "NEW RELEASES" grid of album cards whose covers are generated geometric CSS/SVG art, unique per card; a tracklist table; a tour-dates list with rotated SOLD OUT stamps; and a sign-up box. Interaction: cards physically "press down" on hover/click (shadow collapses, element translates); a sticker you can drag anywhere; a "SHUFFLE COVERS" button that re-rolls the cover art; and a "preview" button that plays a short synthesized drum loop (Web Audio, after a gesture). Must remain highly legible and responsive.

title: Soft Machine
prompt: Create "SOFT MACHINE", a playable neumorphic synthesizer. Everything is sculpted from one soft clay surface (#e4e8ee) with paired light/dark shadows (#ffffff / #b8bec7), raised and pressed states, and a single accent — warm coral #ff6b5a — for active LEDs and the waveform. Layout: a device centred on the page with an OLED-like inset screen showing a live oscilloscope (AnalyserNode drawn on canvas); four rotary knobs (cutoff, resonance, attack, release) dragged vertically; a waveform selector (sine/triangle/saw/square) as neumorphic segmented buttons; a 16-step sequencer row of soft pads; and a two-octave keyboard of soft keys. Typography: a rounded sans stack ("SF Pro Rounded", Nunito, "Varela Round", "Segoe UI", system-ui, sans-serif) with small-caps labels in muted slate. Interaction: click/touch keys or use computer keys A–K to play (Web Audio oscillator → filter → envelope); knobs update the sound in real time with smooth value tooltips; the sequencer plays/stops with adjustable tempo. Audio starts only after the first gesture. Responsive: the device scales down and the keyboard becomes compact on phones without page overflow.

title: The Last Keepers
prompt: Design a long-read editorial feature: "The Last Keepers — Life at the Edge of the Light", a fictional magazine story about lighthouse keepers. Write original, evocative literary prose (~900 words), impressionistic rather than presenting invented facts as real history. Typography-led: a classic book serif ("Iowan Old Style", "Palatino Linotype", Palatino, "P052", Georgia, serif) for body text at a comfortable measure, a large Didone-feeling headline, an ornamental drop cap, small-caps bylines, pull quotes that break the column, and marginal notes on wide screens. Palette: cream paper #f6f1e7, ink navy #14213d, signal red #c0392b, fog grey. Hero: a full-bleed SVG illustration of a lighthouse on rocks at dusk with a rotating light beam that sweeps across the headline and a gently animated sea. Scroll storytelling: sections fade and rise in; a reading-progress bar styled as a lighthouse beam; a section where the background shifts from dusk to night as you scroll; and an illustrated "anatomy of a lens" figure (Fresnel lens rings) that assembles on scroll. Footnotes pop up on click. Must read beautifully on phones.

title: Asterism — Draw Your Own Sky
prompt: Build "Asterism — Draw Your Own Sky", an interactive star chart where you invent constellations. A deep indigo night gradient (#060818 → #141a3d) with a procedurally placed star field (varying magnitude, subtle colour temperature from blue-white to amber, twinkle), a faint Milky Way band made of clustered noise particles, and fine gold line work (#e8c872) in the style of antique celestial atlases. Click one star and then another to draw gold connecting lines; when you close a shape (or press "Name it"), the constellation receives a generated mythic name (combined from curated word lists, e.g. "The Weeping Heron") and an engraved label with a faint illustrated halo appears. A side panel (glass, collapsible on mobile) lists your constellations; hovering highlights them. Also: a slowly rotating sky (drag to rotate), a toggle for a coordinate grid of curved RA/Dec-style lines, "Clear sky" and "Save as PNG". Constellations persist in localStorage. Typography: elegant serif capitals with wide tracking and italic Latin-flavoured subtitles.

title: Mercury
prompt: Create "MERCURY", a hero page for a fictional generative-audio studio whose centrepiece is a liquid chrome blob. On near-black (#050506), render a metaball cluster (canvas or SVG gooey filter) shaded as polished liquid metal — environment-map-like banding in silvers (#e8ecf1, #9aa3ad) and deep blacks with a thin iridescent rim (cyan → magenta → gold). The blobs orbit, merge and split organically; the cursor acts as a magnet, pulling a droplet that stretches and then snaps back with viscous easing. A giant wordmark "MERCURY" in a wide, heavy sans with a chrome gradient fill and a slow specular sweep; the blob passes behind and in front of letters (layering). Minimal navigation, a one-line manifesto, three glass "capability" chips, and a CTA button whose hover makes a small droplet drip from it. Interaction: pointer magnetism, click to split a droplet off, scrolling gently shrinks the blob into the corner. Tasteful, luxurious, silky 60fps; reduced motion shows a static sculpted frame.

title: Herbarium Imaginarium
prompt: Design "Herbarium Imaginarium", a Victorian botanical specimen cabinet of procedurally grown plants that do not exist. Aged paper (#efe6d2 with foxing spots and fibre texture from layered radial gradients), sepia ink (#4a3622), faded botanical greens (#6b7f4e, #9aa77a) and madder-red accents for seeds and berries. Each specimen card shows a plant grown by an L-system/recursive branching algorithm and drawn in SVG with ink-like stroke variation, leaves, buds and occasional flowers; a paper tape strip "holding" the stem; a handwritten-feeling label in an italic serif with an invented Latin binomial (generated from syllable lists), a collection date and a specimen number. A grid of six specimens on desktop, one or two on mobile. Interaction: "Collect a new specimen" grows a plant stroke by stroke (animated stroke-dashoffset); clicking a card opens it large in a lightbox with a magnifying-loupe hover; a "Press" button toggles a flattened pressed-flower look (desaturated, slightly translucent). Typography: "Iowan Old Style", Palatino, "P052", Georgia, serif, with italic labels and ornamental rules.

title: Nimbus — Weather for Port Aurelia
prompt: Build "Nimbus", an elegant weather dashboard for the fictional coastal city of Port Aurelia (clearly fictional sample data). The hero is an animated sky that changes with the selected condition: clear day (drifting sun glare, soft clouds), rain (parallax raindrops, darker gradient), snow (flakes with sway), thunderstorm (lightning flashes) and clear night (stars, moon). The palette adapts per condition but stays sophisticated (e.g. day #7cc4f5 → #e8f6ff, night #0b1026 → #2b2f63). Foreground glass cards: current temperature as a huge thin numeral, feels-like, humidity and UV; an animated wind compass; a sunrise/sunset arc with the sun's current position; a 24-hour temperature line chart (SVG smooth curve with gradient fill and hover tooltip); and a 7-day forecast strip with custom SVG weather icons that animate on hover. Interaction: clicking a forecast day switches the whole scene and its data with a smooth cross-fade; a °C/°F toggle. Typography: a clean sans with tabular numerals.

title: Woolgathering
prompt: Create "Woolgathering", Conway's Game of Life rendered as a living piece of knitting. Each cell is drawn on a canvas as a knit stitch (a small V-shaped pair of loops with shading); live cells are coloured yarn and dead cells are background yarn, so the evolving pattern reads as Fair Isle knitwear. Palette of cosy wools: oatmeal #e9dcc5 background, rust #b5502b, mustard #d9a441, forest #2f5d50, cream #f6efe2 — plus a colourway selector with four palettes. Add a subtle fuzz/halo on stitches and gentle drape shading across the fabric. Frame the canvas as if it hangs from knitting needles (SVG at the top) with yarn-ball illustrations. Warm rounded controls: play/pause, step, speed, randomise, clear, and preset patterns (glider, pulsar, Gosper glider gun, a snowflake motif). Draw cells with pointer or touch. Show the generation count as a knitted row counter. Typography: a friendly serif ("Cooper", Georgia, "URW Bookman", serif).

title: MOVE — A Manifesto in Motion
prompt: Design "MOVE — A Manifesto in Motion", a scroll-driven kinetic typography experience. Black background (#0a0a0a), off-white type (#f1f1ec) and one acid accent (#c6ff00). Seven original manifesto statements about motion, attention and design each get a full-screen scene with a distinct typographic motion driven by scroll progress: letters assembling from scattered positions; words stretching horizontally with scaleX; a line splitting in half to reveal an accent line; characters cascading like dominoes; a word rotating in 3D; a sentence typed out with a caret; and a giant word zooming until its counter becomes the next scene's background. Use sticky sections and custom scroll-progress mapping, with CSS transforms only for performance. Typography: a heavy grotesque/condensed sans stack for display and monospace for small annotations such as scene numbers ("SC. 03 / 07"). A progress rail on the side. Reduced motion: statements appear statically with simple fades.

title: The Aurelian
prompt: Create a landing page for "The Aurelian", a fictional 1928 Art Deco grand hotel. Black lacquer (#0b0b0c) and deep emerald (#0f3d33) grounds with gold (#d4af37, grading to #f5e3a1) geometric ornament — sunbursts, stepped ziggurat frames, chevrons and fan motifs, all inline SVG. Typography: tall, thin, high-contrast display capitals (stack: Didot, "Bodoni 72", "Bodoni MT", "C059", Georgia, serif) with wide letter-spacing, plus refined small caps. Sections: a hero with an animated sunburst radiating behind the hotel name and a symmetrical Deco frame that draws itself in gold; "The Suites" as three arched cards with gilded hover states; a dining section with a menu styled as an engraved card; an elevator-dial floor selector that scrolls to sections while its needle rotates; and a reservation form with Deco-bordered inputs. Delight: a gold-foil shimmer sweeping across headings and fan patterns that open on scroll. Elegant and symmetrical on desktop, gracefully stacked on phones.

title: Plaza Aeterna
prompt: Build "PLAZA AETERNA — Mall of Tomorrow (Est. 1994)", a vaporwave dreamscape. Background: a sunset gradient (#ff71ce → #b967ff → #01cdfe) with a striped retro sun, a 3D-perspective neon grid floor scrolling toward the viewer, palm silhouettes, and a slowly rotating marble bust built from layered SVG shapes with procedurally generated marble veining. Overlay draggable Windows-95-style windows (bevelled grey #c0c0c0, navy title bars) containing: a "Store Directory" with pastel icons, a mock MIDI player that plays a synthesized chord progression (Web Audio, after a gesture), and a "Welcome" message in full-width styling (Ａ Ｅ Ｓ Ｔ Ｈ Ｅ Ｔ Ｉ Ｃ). Typography: a mixture of serif italics, pixel-feeling monospace and widely spaced letters. Interaction: drag windows by their title bars, minimise them to a taskbar with a Start button and clock, click desktop icons to open windows, and a VHS tracking glitch on hover. Responsive: windows become stacked cards on phones.

title: Harmonia — Pendulum Wave
prompt: Create "Harmonia — Pendulum Wave", a physically accurate pendulum-wave simulation as minimalist kinetic art. Charcoal background (#16171b); 18 pendulums whose lengths are chosen so they complete 51, 52, 53… oscillations in 60 seconds (the classic pendulum-wave set-up), rendered from a slightly elevated 3D perspective with fine white strings and glowing spheres in a gradient spectrum from #ffd6a5 to #9bf6ff, plus optional light trails that paint Lissajous-like ribbons. A thin brushed-metal mounting bar at the top. Beneath, an elegant monospace readout: elapsed time, cycle phase, and a timeline scrubber showing where you are in the 60-second pattern (snake, split, chaos, realignment). Controls: play/pause, speed (0.25×–4×), trails toggle, view toggle (side / top-down), and "Release", which pulls every pendulum back and lets them drop. Optional soft chime whenever a pendulum crosses centre (Web Audio pentatonic, after a gesture, muted by default). Typography: thin sans plus mono.

title: Foxglove Hollow
prompt: Design "Foxglove Hollow", a layered paper-cut forest diorama. Seven to nine stacked layers of hand-cut-looking paper (SVG paths with slightly irregular edges) — distant hills, pines, a winding river, mushrooms, ferns, a small fox and foreground grasses — each casting a soft drop shadow onto the layer behind it so the scene has real depth. Day palette: sage #9bb89b, moss #5f7f5b, deep teal #274e52, ochre #d9a45b, burnt orange #c8642d, cream sky #f3e8d2. Night palette: indigo layers, tiny glowing windows, fireflies and a paper moon. Subtle paper grain from procedural noise. Interaction: pointer movement creates parallax between layers (touch-drag on mobile); a day/night toggle recolours every layer with a staggered transition; clicking the fox makes it hop to a new spot; paper leaves drift gently. The title sits on a small paper tag hanging from a string, in a warm serif. The composition must recompute nicely for portrait screens.

title: HELIOS/OS
prompt: Build "HELIOS/OS v2.3", a retro CRT terminal operating system simulation. Full-screen phosphor green (#33ff66 on #031a07) with themes for amber (#ffb000 on #1a0f00) and ice (#9fe7ff). CRT effects in CSS/canvas: scanlines, subtle screen curvature (vignette, rounded corners, inner shadow), phosphor glow/bloom text-shadow, gentle flicker and a rolling refresh bar. On load: a believable BIOS boot sequence (memory check counting up, device list) followed by a login banner. A working shell with an input line and blinking block caret supporting: help, ls, cat <file> (several short fictional files including a poem and a mission log), clear, date, whoami, theme <green|amber|ice>, matrix (glyph rain for a few seconds), weather (ASCII art), snake (a small playable ASCII snake game inside the terminal), command history with ↑/↓, and tab completion. Typography: a monospace stack. Keyboard-first, with tap-to-focus on phones so the soft keyboard appears. Optional typing sounds (Web Audio clicks, off by default).

title: Long Water — The World's Great Rivers
prompt: Create "Long Water — The World's Great Rivers", an elegant data-art visualization comparing the ten longest rivers. Use these commonly cited approximate lengths (label them "approx." and note that sources vary): Nile 6,650 km; Amazon 6,400; Yangtze 6,300; Mississippi–Missouri 6,275; Yenisei 5,539; Yellow River 5,464; Ob–Irtysh 5,410; Paraná 4,880; Congo 4,700; Amur 4,444. Each river is a flowing, meandering SVG ribbon whose length is proportional to its real length, flowing left to right with particles drifting along it like current. Palette: deep river blues and teals on pale limestone (#f3f1ec) — a sequential scale from #0b3d5c to #7fc8c2 — with thin ink labels. Typography: refined serif titles, small-caps continent labels, tabular numerals. Interaction: hover a river to highlight it and show a tooltip (length, continent, where it flows out); sort toggle (by length / by continent); unit toggle (km / miles); a "race" button where droplets travel every river at the same speed so the differences in length can be felt. Include an elegant legend and a short intro paragraph. Mobile: ribbons become vertical flows.

title: Formlehre — Bauhaus Composer
prompt: Build "Formlehre — Bauhaus Composer", a tactile composition toy honouring Bauhaus design. A board on warm cream (#f1ead8) with a tray of primary shapes — circle, square, triangle, semicircle, quarter-circle, bar — in the Bauhaus triad red #d62d20, yellow #f4c20d and blue #1d4e9e, plus black #111. Drag shapes onto the board; they snap to a hidden 8×8 grid with a satisfying spring; rotate with the wheel or R key, scale with handles, recolour by clicking a swatch, bring to front. A "Kandinsky" button auto-composes a balanced composition using Kandinsky's colour–form associations (yellow triangle, red square, blue circle) with a short explanatory caption. Typography: a geometric sans stack (Futura, "Century Gothic", "Avenir Next", "URW Gothic", sans-serif) with lowercase-only headings in the Bayer "universal" spirit and large numeral section markers. The toolbar is made of coloured geometric buttons. Export the composition as PNG. Keyboard: Delete removes, arrows nudge. Works with touch.

title: Descent — Eleven Thousand Metres Down
prompt: Create "Descent — Eleven Thousand Metres Down", a scroll-driven journey from the ocean surface to the bottom of the Mariana Trench (~10,935 m). As you scroll, the background transitions through the ocean zones — sunlight (#1e90c8), twilight (#0b3a66), midnight (#04142b), abyssal (#020812) and hadal (#000204) — while a fixed depth gauge counts metres and shows the zone name, pressure (≈ 1 additional atmosphere per 10 m) and temperature notes. Illustrated SVG/canvas creatures appear at approximately correct depths: dolphins and sunlit fish near the top, jellyfish, a sperm whale (~1,000 m and deeper), an anglerfish with a glowing lure, a vampire squid, a gulper eel, amphipods, and finally the trench floor. Deeper creatures are bioluminescent, with pulsing blue/green light; marine snow drifts through the water; light rays from the surface fade out gradually. Short, accurate captions (keep claims general and well established). Interaction: scroll; in the dark zones the pointer is a faint torch revealing nearby creatures; clicking a creature opens a caption card. It ends with an elegant "Return to surface" button that smooth-scrolls up.

title: Rosette — Symmetry Painter
prompt: Build "Rosette — Symmetry Painter", a radial-symmetry drawing instrument. A black canvas (#070707) where every stroke is mirrored across N rotational segments (selectable 3–24, plus mirror on/off) around the centre, producing mandala-like jewel artwork. Brushes: glowing neon line (additive blending), ink line with velocity-based width, dotted stardust, and ribbon. Palette presets: "Jewels" (#ff006e #fb5607 #ffbe0b #8338ec #3a86ff), "Byzantine" (golds and deep blues), "Porcelain" (cobalt on white — switches the background to white), plus a hue-cycling rainbow mode. A faint guide shows the segment lines while drawing and fades out afterwards. UI: a floating, elegant control dock (glass on dark) with segment slider, brush picker, palette swatches, undo, clear (with a dissolve animation) and PNG download. Delight: an idle "autodraw" that paints slowly on its own until the user touches the canvas, and a gentle rotation mode that spins the artwork. Touch-friendly with pointer capture.

title: Maison Varenne — Calibre 01
prompt: Design a product page for "Maison Varenne — Calibre 01", a fictional minimalist luxury watch. Palette: ivory #f5f1ea, champagne #d8c3a5, charcoal #1c1c1c and a hint of midnight blue #1b2a41 for a dial variant. The hero is a large, photoreal-feeling SVG watch built entirely from gradients: a brushed-steel case with conical highlights, a domed sapphire reflection, applied indices with tiny shadows, dauphine hands showing the REAL current local time, and a smoothly sweeping seconds hand (8 beats per second). Typography: a refined high-contrast serif for headings with wide-tracked small sans captions. Sections with generous whitespace: an exploded view of the movement whose layers separate on scroll; a dial variant selector (ivory / midnight / salmon) that recolours the watch with a smooth transition; a specification table; and a "Reserve" CTA. Interaction: hovering the watch tilts it slightly and moves the sapphire reflection; a "Night" toggle shows lume glowing on the hands and indices. Quiet, precise animation — nothing gaudy.

title: Pocket Metropolis
prompt: Create "Pocket Metropolis", an isometric tiny-city builder toy. A canvas-rendered isometric grid (12×12 on desktop, fitted on mobile) in soft pastels: grass #a8d5a2, water #7ec8e3, roads #d6d0c4, and buildings in peach #ffb5a7, blush #fcd5ce, mint #b8e0d2 and lavender #cdb4db, with gentle ambient-occlusion shading on each block face. A bottom toolbar places houses, towers, trees, parks, roads and water; buildings pop in with a squash-and-stretch bounce. Little cars travel along connected road tiles and tiny people stroll in parks. A day/night cycle slowly shifts the lighting (sky gradient behind, windows lighting up at night, glowing streetlamps). A stats bubble shows population and happiness (parks near homes increase it). Interaction: click/tap tiles to place; right-click/long-press to bulldoze with a puff of dust; drag to pan; pinch/scroll to zoom; "Random town" seeds a charming city. Persist to localStorage. Typography: a rounded, friendly sans.

title: PULSE — Generative Audio Visualizer
prompt: Build "PULSE — Generative Audio Visualizer". On first click, a built-in generative electronic track starts, synthesized entirely with Web Audio (kick, hi-hat from filtered noise, a bassline and an arpeggiated pad in a minor key at ~110 BPM, evolving every 8 bars). An AnalyserNode drives the centrepiece: a radial frequency bloom — 128 bars around a circle with mirrored symmetry, a pulsating core that swells on each kick, orbiting particles that accelerate with high frequencies, and a smoky trail (canvas feedback with a slight zoom/rotation each frame). Before audio starts, an idle breathing version of the visual must already look beautiful. Palette: sunset-to-violet gradient (#ff9a3c → #ff3c78 → #7b2ff7 → #16d9e3) on deep plum-black #0c0612. Typography: wide, spaced uppercase sans for the title and a small monospace readout of BPM, bar count and track section. Controls: play/pause; mode switch between "Bloom", "Tunnel" (concentric rings rushing toward the viewer) and "Horizon" (mirrored waveform landscape); volume. Optional "Use microphone" button with a graceful fallback if permission is denied.

title: Senbazuru — Fold a Paper Crane
prompt: Create "Senbazuru — Fold a Paper Crane", an animated, step-by-step origami crane made with CSS 3D transforms or canvas 3D projection. A square of patterned washi paper (generated seigaiha waves or asanoha pattern in indigo #264653 on cream, with a coral #e76f51 reverse side) folds through about eight key stages — square base, bird base, narrowing folds, head fold, wings — with smooth hinge rotations, correct front/back faces and soft directional shading on each facet that changes with its angle. A clean Japanese-minimal layout: off-white #f7f3ec, lots of space, the step number as a large thin numeral, a one-line instruction for each step, and a progress rail of eight dots. Interaction: next/previous buttons, arrow keys and an auto-play toggle; drag to orbit the model; a picker for three washi patterns. Finale: the finished crane flaps gently and floats above a soft shadow while a counter reads "1 of 1000". Typography: an elegant serif plus tiny wide-tracked sans labels.

title: Elementa
prompt: Design "Elementa", an interactive periodic table of all 118 elements with a premium dark look (#0d1117). Each tile shows atomic number, symbol and name, coloured by category with a harmonious palette (alkali metals #ff6b6b, alkaline earth #ffa94d, transition metals #ffd43b, post-transition #69db7c, metalloids #38d9a9, nonmetals #4dabf7, halogens #748ffc, noble gases #da77f2, lanthanides #f783ac, actinides #e599f7) at soft opacity with glowing borders. Use standard atomic weights, rounded sensibly. The layout follows the standard 18-column table with the f-block below; on narrow phones the table pans horizontally inside its own scroll container (the page itself must not overflow). Interaction: hovering or focusing a tile fills a large detail panel with an animated Bohr-model shell diagram (electrons orbiting on shells with correct per-shell counts), category, atomic mass and state at room temperature; the category legend buttons filter and highlight; a search box jumps to an element. Keyboard navigable with arrow keys.

title: Carriage Return — A Typewriter for Letters
prompt: Build "Carriage Return — A Typewriter for Letters", an interactive typewriter writing experience featuring a fictional machine, the "Marlowe 44". A three-quarter illustrated typewriter (SVG; mint-green enamel #9fc9b6 with cream keys and chrome details) sits at the bottom, and a sheet of textured paper (#faf6ec) feeds out above it. Typing on the physical keyboard (or tapping on-screen keys) stamps characters onto the paper with realistic imperfections: slight baseline jitter, varied ink density, an occasional faint double strike, ribbon texture. The carriage visibly shifts left as you type, a bell dings near the right margin, and Enter triggers a carriage return with the lever animation and a line feed. Synthesized sounds (Web Audio clicks and bell) after the first gesture, with a mute toggle. title: Orbital — N-Body Gravity Playground

title: Frost Garden — Diffusion-Limited Aggregation

title: Nonna Lucia's Lemon Ricotta Tart
prompt: Design "Nonna Lucia's Lemon Ricotta Tart", a beautiful interactive recipe page. title: Midnight Window

title: Infinite Coastline — Mandelbrot & Julia Explorer

title: Atelier Noire — Autumn/Winter

title: Selene — Tide & Moon Clock
prompt: Create "Selene — Tide & Moon Clock", a poetic instrument showing today's moon phase and a stylised tidal cycle. title: Tend — A Habit Garden

title: Vast — A Scroll Across the Solar System

title: Squishy — Claymorphism UI Kit

title: Riso Lab — Halftone Print Studio

title: Hytte — A Winter Cabin

A title placard in a Scandinavian-style serif. The composition adapts to portrait screens (window above, fireplace below).

title: Helix — The Double Helix Explained
prompt: Build "Helix — The Double Helix Explained", an educational, beautiful interactive visualization. title: Arcana Nocturne — A Three-Card Reading
prompt: Create "Arcana Nocturne — A Three-Card Reading". title: ELASTIC — Letterforms on Springs
prompt: Build "ELASTIC — Letterforms on Springs", an experimental typography playground. A giant word (default "BOUNCE", editable via an input) is converted into points sampled from its glyphs (draw the text on an offscreen canvas and sample filled pixels); each point is tied to its home position by a spring. Click to explode the word into particles that reassemble. Palette: hot magenta #ff2e88 on deep ink #111018, with cyan #29e7cd on fast-moving points (velocity-coloured). Modes: dots; lines (connecting nearby neighbours); threads (points tied to home with visible springs). Sliders: stiffness, damping, force radius. title: Dune Engine — Falling Sand Sandbox

title: Radical Shapes — Milano Design Fest '86
prompt: Design "RADICAL SHAPES — Milano Design Fest '86" (fictional), a Memphis-Group-inspired event landing page. Palette: black #111, pink #ff90b3, turquoise #2ec4b6, yellow #ffd23f, lilac #b388eb, red #ef476f on white, with terrazzo/confetti patterns and squiggle backgrounds (SVG patterns). The composition is bold, playful and asymmetric: geometric objects (cylinders, zigzags, dotted triangles, half-moons) float and rotate slowly around the hero title. Typography: chunky geometric sans headlines, bold outlines and two-colour offset text shadows. Sections: a countdown to the fictional opening with flip digits; a lineup of fictional designers on cards with patterned headers; a schedule timeline; a venue map made of playful illustrated blocks; and ticket tiers. Interaction: shapes bounce away from the cursor; clicking the hero spawns new random Memphis shapes with a pop; cards wobble on hover; a pattern-shuffler button changes every background pattern. Keep chaos from overwhelming readability: a strong grid underneath.

title: Karesansui — A Zen Sand Garden
prompt: Create "Karesansui — A Zen Sand Garden": a top-down view of a raked gravel garden on canvas with fine sand texture (#e8e0cf with grain noise and subtle lighting), a few natural stones (procedurally shaped and shaded, with moss patches #6b7d4b) and a wooden border frame (#5b3f2a). Dragging with the rake carves parallel grooves (4–5 tines) that follow your path, with realistic light and shadow on the ridges; the ripple tool draws concentric rings around a stone on click. Tools in a minimal vertical bar: rake, ripple, place stone, smooth (softly erases grooves), and "return to calm" (animated smoothing). Ambient touches: a maple leaf occasionally drifts across and settles; soft shadows move slowly as if the sun were passing; an optional distant wind chime (Web Audio, after a gesture). Typography: small, elegant serif captions and a vertically set title. Touch on mobile is first-class.

title: QUANTA Terminal
prompt: Build "QUANTA Terminal", a dark, premium trading dashboard with clearly fictional tickers and simulated data (labelled "Simulated market"). Near-black ground (#0b0e11), panel surfaces #12161c, gains emerald #16c784, losses crimson #ea3943, gold accent #f0b90b, hairline borders. Layout: a scrolling ticker tape at the top; a main candlestick chart (canvas) with volume bars, moving averages, a crosshair with OHLC tooltip, time-range tabs and smooth panning/zooming; a live order book with depth bars that flicker as orders update; a recent-trades feed; a watchlist with sparklines; a portfolio allocation donut; and a buy/sell ticket with validation and a confirmation toast. Data evolves in real time via a random walk with volatility clustering. Typography: tabular numerals, a clean sans, monospace for prices; prices flash green/red on change. Responsive: panels reflow into tabs on mobile. Smooth and crisp at high DPI.

title: Dusk Meadow — Fireflies
prompt: Create "Dusk Meadow — Fireflies", a tranquil canvas scene. A meadow at dusk: a sky gradient from deep indigo (#141b41) to a very soft dusty rose at the horizon (#e8a0a0), layered silhouettes of rolling hills and a treeline in near-black greens (#0b1a12), and a foreground of hundreds of grass blades swaying in a noise-driven wind field and bending away from the pointer. About 120 fireflies wander with boids-like motion, each blinking on its own rhythm in warm yellow-green (#e8ff8a) with bloom, and slowly synchronising their flashes over time (Kuramoto-style coupling) — a quiet emergent delight. The pointer is a gentle lantern: fireflies drift toward it when it is held still and scatter when it moves fast. A crescent moon rises slowly and stars appear as the sky darkens. Minimal controls at the bottom-left that fade when idle: sync strength, wind, and sound (synthesized crickets). Title in a delicate italic serif.

title: GROOVY — Lava Lamp
prompt: Build "GROOVY — Lava Lamp", a 1970s lava lamp rendered with real metaball physics. A classic lamp silhouette (chrome/gold base and cap drawn in SVG with metallic gradients) centred on warm retro wallpaper (repeating SVG pattern of orange/brown circles, #f4a259, #bc4b51, #5b8e7d on #f4e1c1). Inside the glass, wax blobs heated at the bottom rise, cool and sink, merging and splitting (metaball field computed on a low-resolution grid with smooth thresholded edges, glossy highlights and inner glow). Colour combinations: "Classic" (red wax in yellow liquid), "Purple Haze" (magenta in blue), "Lime" (green in violet) and "Ocean". Interaction: click the lamp's switch to turn it on/off (the light fades, the wax slows and settles); a temperature knob; a colour-combo switch; the pointer heats the glass locally. The whole room's glow is tinted by the lamp colour. Typography: a groovy rounded bold display with an outline shadow.

title: Skyward — A Brief History of Flight
prompt: Design "Skyward — A Brief History of Flight", an interactive horizontal timeline. Sky palette: dawn blue #bde0fe, cerulean #3a86ff, cloud white, sunset accent #ff8fab, ink #1d3557. A long drag-scrollable (and wheel/keyboard) timeline from 1783 to 1969 with well-established milestones: 1783 first crewed hot-air balloon flight (Montgolfier brothers' balloon); 1853 Cayley's crewed glider; 1891 Lilienthal's gliders; 1903 the Wright Flyer at Kitty Hawk (12 seconds, 120 feet); 1909 Blériot crosses the English Channel; 1919 Alcock and Brown make the first non-stop transatlantic flight; 1927 Lindbergh's solo transatlantic flight; 1932 Amelia Earhart's solo transatlantic flight; 1939 first jet-powered flight (Heinkel He 178); 1947 Chuck Yeager breaks the sound barrier in the Bell X-1; 1957 Sputnik 1; 1961 Yuri Gagarin orbits Earth; 1969 Apollo 11 lands on the Moon. Each milestone has an elegant SVG line illustration of the craft, its date and a short caption. Parallax clouds at several depths; a small paper plane travels along the timeline. Clicking a milestone expands its card. A progress altimeter shows the year. Typography: an aviation-inspired sans with serif captions.

title: Fridge Verse — Magnetic Poetry
prompt: Build "Fridge Verse — Magnetic Poetry", a tactile word-magnet toy. A large enamel fridge door (subtle vertical gradient #eef0f2 with faint metallic noise and a chrome handle at the side) holding about 120 word magnets: small white tiles (#fffdf7) with a slight drop shadow and a serif word, each rotated slightly at random, a few coloured (pale pink, mint, butter) for flair. Choose a vocabulary (nouns, verbs, adjectives, suffixes -s, -ing, -ed) that makes poetic combinations likely. Dragging a magnet gives a pleasing lift (shadow grows, slight rotation) and a snap back onto the door; magnets may overlap. Features: a "Shake" button that scatters magnets with physics; theme packs (Love, Ocean, Space, Kitchen); a poem detector that reads tiles arranged in lines left to right and shows the current poem in a small card you can copy; a few decorative fridge items (a drawn polaroid picture, a fruit magnet). Persist positions in localStorage. Typography: classic serif tiles with a rounded sans for the UI.

title: Patchwork — A Generative Quilt
prompt: Create "Patchwork — A Generative Quilt". Every visit (and every click on "Stitch a new quilt") generates a unique quilt made from traditional blocks — Log Cabin, Flying Geese, Half-Square Triangles, Nine Patch, Pinwheel, Churn Dash, Ohio Star — laid out on a grid with sashing and borders. Fabrics are procedural SVG patterns: gingham, calico florals (tiny flower motifs), polka dots, stripes and chambray, in warm cottage palettes (e.g. barn red #9e2a2b, mustard #e09f3e, denim #335c67, cream #fff3b0, sage #9fb8ad). Visible dashed stitching, slight puffy shading on each patch (quilted look via inner shadows) and a wavy binding edge. Interaction: hovering a block lifts it slightly and shows its pattern name; clicking cycles its pattern; a palette chooser (Farmhouse, Indigo, Sunset, Scandinavian); a "drape" toggle shows the quilt hanging on a line, waving gently in the wind. Download PNG. Typography: a warm serif with an embroidery-like dashed underline.

title: Planet Forge — Procedural World Generator
prompt: Build "Planet Forge — Procedural World Generator". A canvas renders a rotating sphere with per-pixel shading (ray–sphere intersection or a pre-baked equirectangular texture sampled by rotation): terrain from fractal noise mapped to biomes (deep ocean, shallows, beaches, forests, deserts, mountains, ice caps by latitude), an animated cloud layer, an atmospheric rim glow, a day/night terminator with city lights on the night side, and optional rings casting a shadow. A cosmic black background with a faint nebula and stars. A sci-fi control panel (thin lines, cyan #4cc9f0 accents, glass panels) with sliders for sea level, temperature, cloud cover, terrain roughness, ring toggle, moon count, rotation speed and seed, plus presets (Earthlike, Desert world, Ocean world, Lava world, Ice world, banded Gas giant). Each planet receives a catalogue designation (e.g. "KX-4471 b") and playful stats. Interaction: drag to rotate, "Randomize", PNG download. Keep rendering efficient (render at lower resolution and upscale smoothly).

title: ASCII TIDES
prompt: Create "ASCII TIDES", an animated ocean scene made entirely of monospace characters rendered into a <pre> or a canvas character grid. Characters map to wave height and foam (e.g. " .,:;~=≈*#@"). Layers: a sky with slowly drifting ASCII clouds and a sun or moon made of characters, a horizon, rolling swells (sum of sines plus noise), foam crests, and a small character-built boat bobbing on the surface. Pointer/touch disturbances create ripples that propagate across the water (2D wave equation on the grid). A time-of-day slider changes the sky (stars at night). Typography: a monospace stack with tight line-height; the grid adapts to the viewport to keep characters crisp. A tiny caption in the corner inside an ASCII box-drawing frame. Smooth at 30–60fps with efficient string building.

title: Mira Okafor — Bento Portfolio
prompt: Design a bento-grid portfolio for "Mira Okafor — Product Designer" (fictional). title: Apiary — The Honeycomb
prompt: Build "Apiary — The Honeycomb", an interactive hexagonal-grid artwork. The screen fills with hexagonal cells (canvas or SVG) in honey tones — amber #f6a821, gold #ffc93c, deep honey #c77d0a, wax #fff1c1 — with dark comb gaps (#2a1a05). Cells have a subtle inner bevel and translucency: some are filled with glowing honey (animated fill level with a meniscus shine), others are empty wax, a few are capped. title: Grandmaster's Study
prompt: Create "Grandmaster's Study", an elegant, playable two-player chess board (local hot-seat). A luxurious board of maple (#e8d0aa) and walnut (#8a5a3b) squares with subtle wood-grain gradients, a lacquered frame with brass corner fittings, and file/rank coordinates engraved in serif. Pieces drawn in SVG as original Staunton-inspired silhouettes — ivory (#f7f0e1, warm shading) and ebony (#1e1b18, soft highlights). Full legal chess rules: legal move generation with check detection, castling, en passant, promotion (with a chooser), and checkmate/stalemate detection. UX: click or drag pieces; legal moves shown as subtle dots/rings; last move highlighted; check shown as a red glow on the king; a move list in algebraic notation in a side panel styled like a score sheet; a captured-pieces tray; undo; flip board; new game. Smooth gliding piece animations and a soft synthesized "clack" on each move (toggle). Responsive: the board fits the width on phones with the panel below. Typography: a classic serif.

title: Chroma — Colour Palette Studio
prompt: Build "Chroma — Color Palette Studio", an elegant tool for generating harmonious palettes. A clean white UI (#ffffff, #f4f4f5 panels, #18181b text). The main view is five tall colour columns filling the screen (horizontal bands on mobile); each shows hex, RGB, HSL and a name (nearest match from a curated list of ~150 named colours) and has lock, copy and adjust controls. Space (or a button) generates a new palette that respects locked colours using harmony rules — analogous, complementary, split-complementary, triadic, tetradic, monochromatic — computed in OKLCH for perceptual evenness (implement the conversion). Extra panels: a WCAG AA/AAA contrast checker for text on each colour; a live preview card (a mini UI mockup) using the palette; a gradient preview; and export (CSS variables, JSON) copied to the clipboard. Interaction: drag columns to reorder, click a hex to edit it, and a colour-wheel diagram showing the harmony geometry with draggable points. Smooth colour transitions. Typography: a crisp sans plus monospace.

title: Somewhere Inside
prompt: Create "Somewhere Inside", a double-exposure art piece: a large human profile silhouette (a smooth SVG path of a face in profile with shoulders) acts as a mask revealing a whole landscape inside it — layered mountain ranges, a pine forest, a lake reflecting the moon, drifting fog and birds — while outside the silhouette is a pale misty gradient. Palette: a dusk gradient inside (#1d2b53 → #7e2553 → #ff9e7d), mist outside (#f2efe9 → #d9d4cc), ink details. The inner landscape moves in subtle parallax with the pointer (and slowly on its own), fog layers drift, and the moon's reflection shimmers. Original poetic text fragments fade in and out beside the profile in an elegant italic serif. Interaction: pointer parallax; clicking cycles the inner landscape between "Mountains", "Ocean" (waves and a lighthouse) and "City" (skyline with lights), each with its own palette and a smooth cross-fade. A film-grain overlay. The composition reflows for mobile, with the silhouette scaled and centred.

title: Silicon — Living Circuit Board
prompt: Build "Silicon — Living Circuit Board". An SVG printed circuit board in rich green solder mask (#0a4d2e with subtle texture) with gold traces and pads (#d4a537 with highlights), white silkscreen labels (component references such as U1, R12, C4, "REV 2.1"), chips (black epoxy with pin legs and printed markings), capacitors, resistors with colour bands, LEDs and a crystal oscillator. Signals — glowing pulses of cyan (#3cf2ff) and warm white light — travel along traces from chip to chip, routed along a graph of trace segments. Interaction: hovering a component highlights all of its connected traces and shows a spec tooltip; a "power" switch boots the board (LEDs light in sequence, a small OLED component shows boot text); clicking a chip "overclocks" it (faster pulses, a slight heat shimmer); a "logic probe" cursor mode shows voltage readings on traces. A title block in silkscreen monospace in the corner. Scales responsively via viewBox.

title: Iridescence — Soap Bubbles
prompt: Create "Iridescence — Soap Bubbles". A soft, bright sky (#dbeafe → #fef3f2 gradient with faint drifting clouds). Bubbles of varied sizes float upward and drift on a gentle wind, wobbling as their shape oscillates; each is rendered with thin-film interference colours — swirling bands of magenta, gold, cyan and green on a mostly transparent sphere — plus a bright window-shaped specular highlight and a smaller secondary one, with the swirl animating over time (canvas gradients and noise-driven hue shifts). Bubbles collide softly. Interaction: clicking/tapping a bubble pops it — it bursts into a ring of tiny droplets and a quick shimmering film fragment, with a soft "pop" (Web Audio, after the first gesture); dragging blows a new bubble from a wand (it grows with drag distance and detaches on release); wind direction follows pointer movement. A tiny, elegant "bubbles popped" counter. Typography: an airy light sans title that is itself slightly iridescent.

title: Brush & Ink — Calligraphy Pad
prompt: Build "Brush & Ink — Calligraphy Pad". A sheet of rice paper (#f5f0e1 with visible fibres and an optional faint grid of practice squares) on a dark wood desk (#2b1d14), with an inkstone and a brush illustrated at the side. Drawing produces convincing brush strokes: width responds to speed (slow = thick, fast = thin) and to pointer pressure when available; ink runs out over a long stroke, producing dry-brush "flying white" texture; stroke ends taper; ink bleeds slightly into the paper (a subtle blurred halo). Ink colours: sumi black, diluted grey and vermillion. Tools: brush size, ink wetness, undo, clear (the paper slides away and a fresh sheet slides in), a red seal stamp you can place (SVG seal with generated square characters), and PNG download. Include a "trace" mode that shows faint model strokes of a simple character (e.g. 永) to practise over. Typography: small, elegant serif labels with vertical-text accents.

title: ARES VII Mission Control
prompt: Create "ARES VII Mission Control", a dashboard for a fictional crewed Mars mission with clearly simulated telemetry. Aesthetic: "NASA-punk" — dark slate panels (#0e1116), safety orange #ff6b1a, off-white #e8e6e3, amber warnings #ffb000, cyan data #4ee1ff, thin grid lines, rounded-rectangle panels with corner brackets and tiny monospace labels. Panels: a mission elapsed time (MET) counter and a countdown to orbit insertion; a trajectory diagram (SVG Hohmann transfer between Earth and Mars with the spacecraft moving along it); live telemetry charts (cabin O₂, CO₂ ppm, power, velocity) as smoothly scrolling line charts; crew status cards with heart-rate waveforms; a comms log whose messages arrive after a one-way light-time delay; a subsystem status grid with nominal/caution/warning lights; and an animated spacecraft schematic. Interaction: click subsystems for detail; an "acknowledge" button when a random caution appears (flashing, with a Web Audio beep after a gesture); a toggle between Earth time and Mars sol time. A responsive grid that collapses gracefully.

title: The Glass Alibi
prompt: Build "The Glass Alibi", a short interactive film-noir detective story (original, about six scenes with branching choices and two or three endings). Black-and-white visuals with dramatic chiaroscuro: venetian-blind shadow bands sweeping across the scene, rain streaking the window (canvas), a flickering desk lamp, a steaming coffee cup, film grain and vignette overlays, and occasional old-film frame jitter. Scenes are illustrated with SVG silhouettes (office, rainy alley, jazz club, pier) in greys, with a single accent colour reserved for the key clue (a red lipstick mark #b3001b). Narration and dialogue appear with a typewriter effect in a period serif; choices are presented as typed index cards. Include an ambient sound toggle (synthesized rain and a low, jazzy bass line). Features: a case-file notebook that collects clues, iris-wipe scene transitions, and restart. Typography: a Courier-like monospace for notes and a condensed serif for titles.

title: Four Seasons — A Fractal Tree
prompt: Create "Four Seasons — A Fractal Tree", a generative tree swaying in the wind whose appearance follows a seasons slider. Trunk and branches are grown recursively (randomised angles, tapering widths, gentle curvature) and drawn on canvas with bark colouring; noise-driven wind bends branches in proportion to their depth. Seasons: Spring (pale blossoms #ffc8dd and fresh green buds), Summer (a lush green canopy #52b788 with dappled light), Autumn (leaves turning #e76f51, #f4a261, #e9c46a and falling with tumbling physics to pile on the ground) and Winter (bare branches, snow accumulating on limbs, snowfall). Sky and ground transition smoothly with the season. Interaction: drag the slider (or press "Play the year" for a 60-second cycle); click the tree to shake it (leaves or snow fall); "New seed" grows a new tree with a growth animation. Typography: a gentle serif title with month names around a small circular season dial.

title: Pulsar Ridges
prompt: Build "Pulsar Ridges", an animated, original piece in the spirit of classic stacked ridge-line plots. Black background (#000) with ~60 stacked white lines (#f5f5f5) drawn on canvas with occlusion (each line filled black beneath so nearer lines hide farther ones); each profile comes from layered noise plus a central peak region and animates continuously, so the ridges roll like a landscape of signals. Interaction: the pointer position becomes the source of the peaks (ridges swell toward the cursor); clicking switches data modes: "Pulsar" (sharp central peaks), "Terrain" (mountain noise), "Audio" (a built-in synthesized drone analysed with an AnalyserNode drives the lines, after a gesture) and "Heartbeat" (ECG-like spikes). Settings: line count, amplitude, speed, colour mode (white, amber, spectrum gradient). Minimal typography: a small, uppercase, widely tracked monospace caption at the bottom like an album credit. PNG download. Perfectly crisp on high-DPI screens.

title: Luminote — Piano with Falling Lights
prompt: Create "Luminote — Piano with Falling Lights". A full-width three-octave piano keyboard along the bottom (glossy black and ivory keys with realistic depth and pressed states), playable by mouse/touch (multi-touch) and computer keyboard (two rows mapped). Above it, a dark stage (#0a0a12) where notes fall toward the keys like a rhythm-game visualizer: glowing rounded bars coloured by pitch (a soft chromatic rainbow), with sparks and a light burst when they land. Sound: a pleasant piano-like tone synthesized with Web Audio (several detuned harmonics, fast attack, exponential decay, and reverb from a convolver with a generated noise impulse). Modes: "Free play" — played notes rise as light trails; "Listen" — auto-plays public-domain melodies (Ode to Joy, the opening of Für Elise, Twinkle Twinkle Little Star, the opening of Gymnopédie No. 1) with falling notes; "Learn" — the song waits for you to press the right key. Tempo slider and a note-name toggle. Typography: a refined sans with small caps.

title: SIGNAL/NOISE
prompt: Design "SIGNAL/NOISE", the portfolio of a fictional glitch artist, "k.oshiro". Stark black #000 and white #fff with RGB channel accents (#ff0040, #00ff9f, #0070ff). The page is intentionally corrupted but controlled: a headline with RGB split and horizontal slice displacement that re-randomises periodically; project thumbnails that are generative canvases (pixel-sorted gradients, datamosh-like block smears, scanline interference) and glitch harder on hover; CRT scanlines and occasional full-screen tear events; a scrolling "corrupted" hex-dump sidebar. Typography: monospace and a heavy grotesk. Despite the chaos, it stays navigable and legible.

title: Rosée — Eau de Parfum
prompt: Create a product page for "Rosée — Eau de Parfum" by a fictional maison. Palette: blush #f4d6d0, rose gold #b76e79 → #e8b4a0, cream #fff8f3, deep plum text #3b1f2b. Typography: a refined high-contrast serif with wide-tracked sans captions.

title: Connected — A Dot-Matrix Globe
prompt: Build "Connected — A Dot-Matrix Globe". A rotating 3D globe rendered on canvas as a sphere of evenly spaced dots (Fibonacci sphere), with bright land dots and faint ocean dots — land determined from an embedded low-resolution land mask (a compact hand-encoded bitmap, e.g. a 72×36 character grid of the continents). Palette: midnight background #050a18, ocean dots #1b2a4a, land dots #5ad1e6 → #a6fff2, arcs in coral #ff6f61 and gold #ffd166. Animated great-circle arcs travel between about fifteen major world cities placed at their real latitude/longitude (London, New York, Tokyo, São Paulo, Lagos, Sydney, Mumbai, Cairo…), each with a glowing head, a fading tail and a pulsing ring on arrival. An atmospheric glow halos the globe. Interaction: drag to rotate with inertia; hover a city dot for its name; click a city to fly the globe round to face it; auto-rotation resumes after idle. A side panel with clearly simulated stats ("connections per second"). Typography: a clean geometric sans.

title: Crystalline — No Two Alike
prompt: Create "Crystalline — No Two Alike", a procedural snowflake generator. Each snowflake grows with 6-fold (dihedral) symmetry using a branching algorithm — main arms with side dendrites, plates and needles that vary with "temperature" and "humidity" parameters, loosely echoing the Nakaya diagram. The hero shows one large flake slowly rotating; below it, a gallery of smaller generated flakes. Background: gentle snowfall of micro-flakes with depth blur. Interaction: "Grow a snowflake" animates growth outward from a hexagonal seed; temperature and humidity sliders show how the form changes (plates at some settings, dendrites at others — keep the explanation light and approximate); clicking a gallery flake enlarges it; each flake gets a catalogue number and date; download as SVG. Typography: a thin, wide-tracked sans with a delicate serif italic.

prompt: Design "Maison Lierre — Botanical Teas, Paris 1899" (a fictional tea house) as an Art Nouveau poster page in the spirit of the era's great poster artists (original artwork, nothing copied). title: Rule 30 — Tapestries of Elementary Cellular Automata
prompt: Build "Rule 30 — Tapestries of Elementary Cellular Automata". Typography: a textile-label serif with monospace numbers.

title: Pages from Juno's Sketchbook
prompt: Create "Pages from Juno's Sketchbook" (a fictional illustrator), a portfolio designed as a physical sketchbook. Dot-grid paper (#fbf8f1 with faint blue dots), graphite lines (#3d3d3d), highlighter yellow (#fff176) and a single red-pencil accent (#d64545). title: Tempus — Hourglass Timer
prompt: Build "Tempus — Hourglass Timer", a beautiful focus timer with a physically simulated hourglass. Two glass bulbs drawn in SVG with realistic reflections inside a turned-wood and brass frame (#6b4226, #c9a227); sand simulated as particles (or a cellular sand grid) flowing through the neck: the top pile drains with a conical dip, a thin stream falls, and a mound builds in the lower bulb with grains tumbling down its slopes. title: SENTINEL — Radar Array
prompt: Create "SENTINEL — Radar Array", a radar/sonar console as polished UI art, set in a clearly fictional scenario. Phosphor green (#39ff88) on dark olive-black (#020a05), with an amber mode. Interaction: click a contact to lock on (target reticle, detailed readout); a range selector (10/25/50 nm) that rescales smoothly; a radar/sonar toggle — sonar switches to a blue-green water palette with pings and a Web Audio ping sound after a gesture. Typography: monospace with stencilled headings.

title: Horologe — The Word Clock
prompt: Build "Horologe — The Word Clock", a typographic clock that spells the current time in words on a grid of letters (an original English layout in the letter-grid clock tradition: "IT IS HALF PAST TEN", five-minute precision plus four corner dots for single minutes). The clock scales to fill any screen while keeping its square grid.

title: Alpenglow — A Day in the Mountains
prompt: Create "Alpenglow — A Day in the Mountains", a parallax landscape that cycles through a full day. Six procedurally generated mountain ridge layers (midpoint displacement) with atmospheric perspective (farther = lighter and bluer), a foreground lake reflecting sky and mountains with gentle ripples, pine silhouettes on the nearest ridge, and birds that occasionally cross. Time of day animates (or is scrubbed with a slider): pre-dawn indigo, sunrise with pink alpenglow on the peaks (#ff9eaa, #ffd6a5), bright noon blues, golden hour, sunset reds, dusk violets, and a starry night with a moon and the occasional meteor. The sun and moon follow arcs; sky gradients interpolate smoothly between keyframes; ridge colours are recomputed for each moment. Interaction: pointer parallax; a time slider with icons; "Play day" (60 seconds); clicking the sky regenerates the mountains from a new seed. Typography: a small, elegant sans showing the current time and a poetic name for each phase ("Blue hour").

title: Ambience — Soundscape Mixer
prompt: Build "Ambience — Soundscape Mixer", a calm app for mixing natural ambient sounds, all synthesized with Web Audio (no audio files): rain (filtered noise plus random droplet clicks), thunder (low noise bursts), wind (band-pass-swept noise), ocean waves (noise with slow amplitude swells), campfire (crackle impulses and a low rumble), forest birds (short FM chirps at random intervals), crickets (pulsed high sine tones), café murmur (band-limited noise through formant-like filters) and a soft drone pad. Presets ("Stormy cabin", "Beach at dusk", "Deep focus"), a master volume, and a sleep timer that fades everything out. The background gradient shifts subtly with the active mix. Typography: a soft humanist sans. Audio starts only after a gesture.

title: Windwalker — A Kinetic Sculpture Simulation
prompt: Create "Windwalker — A Kinetic Sculpture Simulation", inspired by Theo Jansen's wind-walking beach creatures (an original rendering). Simulate the Jansen linkage with its canonical link lengths (a=38, b=41.5, c=39.3, d=40.1, e=55.8, f=39.4, g=36.7, h=65.7, i=49, j=50, k=61.9, l=7.8, m=15), solving every joint position each frame from the crank angle with circle–circle intersections. Draw a multi-legged creature (e.g. 6–12 legs with phase offsets) walking across a beach (sand #e9d8b4, sea #6fb3c7, sky #f0f4f5) in its pale-yellow tube aesthetic (#f4e3a1 tubes with darker joints), with each foot's path traced as the characteristic curve and a wind sail driving it. Interaction: a wind slider (walking speed); a "single leg diagram" toggle showing one linkage with labelled lengths and its foot trajectory; a trace-paths toggle; buttons to add/remove leg pairs; drag to pan along the beach. Parallax clouds and footprints fading in the sand behind it. Typography: an engineering-notebook sans with monospace labels.

title: Aquarelle — Generative Watercolour Landscapes
prompt: Build "Aquarelle — Generative Watercolor Landscapes". Each generation paints a new landscape in convincing watercolour: layered translucent washes built by recursively deforming polygons (many low-alpha layers with jittered edges) for sky gradients, distant hills, mid-ground mountains, a lake, trees as dabbed blobs, and a sun or moon — all on textured cold-press paper (procedural grain, with pigment darkening where it pools at edges). Palettes rotate among seasonal watercolour sets: "Ultramarine & Burnt Sienna", "Sap Green Spring", "Quinacridone Sunset" and "Payne's Grey Winter". The painting sits on a wooden easel/table background. Typography: a delicate serif with a script-like italic.

title: Lines of Force — Magnetic Field Explorer
prompt: Create "Lines of Force — Magnetic Field Explorer". A lab-styled canvas where you place and drag bar magnets (red N / blue S halves, #d62828 / #1d4e89) on a sheet of paper; the field is computed from magnetic dipoles (or magnetic charges at the poles) and rendered in three switchable styles: (1) iron filings — thousands of tiny dark filings aligned with the field, denser where it is stronger, like the classic school experiment on off-white paper; (2) field lines — smooth streamlines traced from the poles with arrowheads, in elegant ink; (3) a heat map of field magnitude in a refined sequential palette. Interaction: drag magnets; rotate with the wheel, R key or a handle; double-click to flip polarity; add/remove magnets; presets (single bar, attracting pair, repelling pair, quadrupole, horseshoe). Short explanatory captions in a sidebar. Palette: steel grey #6c757d, paper #f8f6f1, red/blue poles. Typography: a clean scientific sans.

title: MONOLITH — Architecture & Landscape
prompt: Design "MONOLITH — Architecture & Landscape" (a fictional studio), a brutalist-minimal architecture portfolio: raw concrete surfaces (procedural texture from layered noise with formwork tie-hole dots and board-mark grain) in greys #8d8d8a, #b5b3ad, #d6d4ce and charcoal #262624, with a single accent of oxidised-copper green #4f7f73. title: Harmonograph — A Drawing Machine
prompt: Build "Harmonograph — A Drawing Machine", simulating the Victorian pendulum drawing device. Render a very fine pen line accumulating on cream paper (#f6f1e3) in sepia ink (#3e2c1c) or selectable inks (indigo, oxblood, or gold on black paper). Controls styled as brass knobs and engraved dials: frequencies (with harmonic-ratio presets such as 2:3, 3:4 and near-unison detuning), phases, damping, pen width and speed. "Release pendulums" starts a fresh drawing that animates stroke by stroke; "Randomize" picks tasteful parameters; "Save drawing" downloads a PNG. Show the current ratio as a musical interval name (fifth, fourth). Typography: Victorian scientific-instrument labels in serif small caps.

title: Droste — The Infinite Room
prompt: Build "Droste — The Infinite Room", an endless-zoom artwork: a self-similar scene that zooms forever — a room with a framed picture on the wall that contains the same room, which contains the picture… Render on canvas by drawing the scene recursively at successive scales (each level scaled by the frame ratio), animating the zoom continuously and wrapping seamlessly each time a full level is reached. title: Organic Wave Lab — Ripple Tank
prompt: Create "Organic Wave Lab — Ripple Tank", an interactive wave-interference laboratory. A full-screen 2D wave simulation (discrete wave equation on a grid with damping and absorbing boundaries) rendered with gorgeous shading: a water-like surface lit from above with normal-based highlights, coloured from aqua #3ee6d6 through deep teal #0b4f6c with coral #ff7b6b crests (plus palettes "Lagoon", "Bioluminescent" and "Monochrome ink"). A lab-instrument UI panel (glassy, rounded, organic shapes) with sliders for wave speed, damping and source frequency, plus a probe that plots amplitude over time at a point as a live oscilloscope trace. Performance: a Float32Array grid at reduced resolution, drawn via ImageData and smoothed. Typography: a rounded scientific sans.
